rule: On a head in two-point perspective the turning edge between the front and side planes runs through the brow peak and temple, and the nose underside and upper lip each show their own planes.
Appealing shapes pair a straight side against a curved side; mirrored bulges (sausage, tube, pinch shapes) look lifeless.
The neck opposes the curve of the back (shown by the sternocleidomastoid) and is never a straight tube.
Two lines that just touch (a tangent) flatten depth; one form should overlap the other in a T junction.
